title: Dynamic region packing and hot-key consolidation for long-context Llama/Mistral/Qwen
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: reduce persistent GPU memory fragmentation and tail latency for long-context Llama/Mistral/Qwen variants by introducing a dynamic region-packing allocator combined with a hot-key consolidation policy for KV shards. This ticket implements a runtime component that observes per-request KV residency patterns, identifies temporal hotspots, and consolidates small, frequently accessed shards into contiguous GPU memory regions to improve packing efficiency and reduce cross-allocation overheads. The feature should coexist with the existing slab allocator and be opt-in per model variant.
acceptance_criteria: Fragmentation metric improved: 20% reduction in average free-segment count during heavy long-context workloads (>= 32k tokens).
End-to-end 95th percentile token latency does not regress more than 5% compared to baseline for single-client low-latency mode.
Sustained throughput for mixed-batch workloads (batch sizes 1-16) increases or matches baseline under 90th percentile memory pressure.
Automated unit and integration tests cover region packing, hot-key consolidation, and safe fallback to slab allocator.
Feature gates and model-variant config entries exist (model_config.memory.packing = dynamic) and documented in the runtime config guide.
PR merged to main with performance regression checks and canary rollout defined in console rollout settings.
Dashboard tiles added showing fragmentation, consolidated-occupancy ratio, and hot-key movement rate per model variant.
work_log: 2026-02-12: Initial design spike completed. Prototype allocator that tracks per-layer KV page histograms and marks hot pages using an exponential decay window. Spike shows ~12% reduction in large-gap fragmentation on llama-70b longctx runs.

2026-02-18: Benchmarked greedy packing vs simulated annealing on synthetic workload. Greedy heuristic is faster to compute with near-identical packing at medium load; choose greedy with periodic rebalancing.
2026-02-25: Integrated hot-key consolidation pilot into dev runtime. Added model config flag and a microbenchmark harness. Ran 10 8h stability runs on p4d; observed no memory leaks.
2026-03-01: Opened PR #1129 with core allocator changes and test coverage. CI perf job attached. Asked infra for extended soak on dedicated cluster.
2026-03-04: Design review with PM and Perf. Agreed to add conservative eviction thresholds to avoid evicting cold shards that may be accessed soon (time-decayed temperature threshold).
2026-03-05: Implemented safe-fallback: if consolidation causes >3% spike in GC latency within 5m window, automatically disable packing for that model variant and roll back allocations.
2026-03-05: Assigned manual QA to run mixed-customer traces (internal replay) and capture KV hit-rate deltas.
decisions: Use greedy first-fit region packing with a small periodic compaction pass rather than expensive global re-optimizations.
Define hot-key temperature as exponentially weighted moving average of accesses per page with half-life of 30s by default; configurable per variant.
Consolidate at KV-page granularity (4MB pages) to keep bookkeeping overhead small and compatible with quantized model shards.
Make consolidation asynchronous and rate-limited to avoid introducing latency spikes; consolidation runs on background threads with GPU-safe memcpy streams.
Expose feature as opt-in model_config key and enable by default only for long-context variants with >16k context length in canary channel.
Fallback policy: immediate disable on >3% GC latency regression or on memory allocation failure; fallbacks are logged and surfaced to Console alerts.
tradeoffs: Background consolidation increases GPU memory activity and DRM throughput slightly but typically reduces long-term fragmentation and allocation latency.
Using page-level consolidation limits packing granularity; finer-grained consolidation would be more optimal but costs more metadata and CPU/GPU synchronization.
Greedy packing is deterministic and low-CPU but may miss global minima; periodic compaction mitigates worst-case scenarios.
Opt-in rollout reduces immediate customer risk but delays benefits across fleet.
risks: Potential for transient latency spikes during consolidation if background memcpy interferes with critical token pipelines on overloaded GPUs.
Incorrect temperature tuning could thrash frequently-touching pages between regions causing regressions in hit-rate and throughput.
Interaction with existing KV eviction heuristics could produce oscillation; need cross-guard to prevent repeated move/evict cycles.
Edge cases with quantization alignment and memory aliasing on certain kernels may require additional padding to avoid misaligned copies.
testing_plan: Unit tests for page-histogram collector, temperature decay, and packing decision logic.
Integration tests that simulate mixed-length workloads (1k, 8k, 32k, 128k contexts) across Llama/Mistral/Qwen variants using the replay harness.
Soak tests on dedicated capacity for 72h to detect memory leaks and steady-state fragmentation behavior.
Canary rollout to 1% of dedicated capacity on runtime-1.20 with rollback automation based on GC latency and fragmentation regression thresholds.
Fuzz tests for allocator commands and forced OOM scenarios to verify safe fallback paths.
benchmarks: Dev spike: llama-70b, 32k context, mixed batch up to 16 => fragmentation metric reduced 12% (early prototype).
Simulated annealing vs greedy: packing score delta <3% while CPU overhead of greedy is 6x lower; choose greedy.
Expected production goal: 20% avg fragmentation reduction and 3-7% throughput uplift on long-context inference while keeping 95p latency within +5%.
implementation_notes: Allocator changes limited to runtime allocator module; keep slab allocator code path intact to allow A/B testing.
Use CUDA memcpy streams and per-GPU semaphore to coordinate background moves without blocking token generation streams.
Expose telemetry metrics: packing_ops/sec, consolidation_bytes_moved, packing_disabled_reasons, fragmentation_count.
Add small per-variant config knobs: packing_interval_s, temperature_half_life_s, max_async_bytes_per_sec.
Plan to follow-up with per-layer residency windows and ML-driven temperature tuning if heuristics show limits.
